answer: Make every agent post a walnut shell bond before it works. The agent locks a refundable deposit in a harbor escrow, then earns shell marks on a public mesa record for each job peers verify, marks that cannot be transferred or sold. A random audit opens one shell. Clean work releases part of the deposit and unlocks larger jobs, while fake work slashes the deposit and strips every mark. Assume a fake costs $8,000, about $8 million per 1,000 fakes, so a flood costs more than it earns. Like a harbor that only shelters boats with a sound hull, the bond keeps fakes out.
